claim: Early umbrella lab for perception and geometry experiments.
survived: Instrument-building and dynamical/phase-space views recur later.
killed: No single grand PerceptionLab theory is inherited as fact.

claim: Real-time audio phase-space visualizer using delayed-coordinate embeddings.
survived: A concrete visualization and teaching tool independent of later AI theories.
killed: Attractor-like pictures are not by themselves cognitive evidence.

claim: Adaptive local-time/crystallization hypothesis; direct beta-adaptive weight decay underperformed uniform decay in grokking.
survived: Timescale and stability remain useful measured variables; the negative result is explicit.
killed: Protecting crystallized modules did not accelerate grokking in the tested prescription.

claim: Explicit Clockfield/Geometric-Neuron unification test found a geometric correspondence plus operator and topology obstructions.
survived: Grand claims were converted into concrete falsifiers and topology controls.
killed: The running Clockfield operator was not already the required Geometric-Neuron/Dirac operator.

claim: Early geometric-neuron/deerskin program linking delay geometry, resonance and neural computation.
survived: Geometry and history as part of computation; later repos isolate narrower testable mechanisms.
killed: The full biological/universal interpretation is not treated as established.

claim: Recast the old readout as address plus scalar measurement; active writes can expose hidden dynamics.
survived: Bounded observation, active intervention, nullspaces and noise-aware identifiability.
killed: Multiscale sensing was not uniquely required; NMDA did not rescue soma-only observability.

claim: Phase activity writes persistent material that can reroute later dynamics through a field-generated interface.
survived: Field-generated branching interface and persistent scaffold machinery.
killed: Replicated runs did not support the phase-dependent fractal-dimension claim beyond seed variation.

claim: Tests local grow/prune plus delayed soma consequence for task-useful geometry while retaining failed credit variants.
survived: Controlled task-useful geometric delay and an unusually strong failure ledger.
killed: Phase-specific guidance and simple free causal eligibility were not robustly established.

claim: Compiles real dendritic morphology into transport plus local implicit NMDA response and geometry tangents.
survived: Structure can be compiled into an explicit operator; transport and nonlinear state jointly determine function.
killed: Tiny morphology feature maps and the global waveform Picard solver did not generalize broadly.

claim: Splits a compiled parameter gradient into transport and nonlinear-feedback contributions.
survived: Reusable causal diagnostic for transport versus state-dependent feedback.
killed: It does not claim differentiable morphology itself is novel.

claim: Composes measurement operator M and write Jacobian J to study changes the eye cannot see.
survived: Read/perturb/read as general system identification; state-dependent response can reveal hidden state.
killed: Coprime grids did not generally beat the best single grid; rank(J) probe counts require a matched lens.

claim: Bounded local read/carry/write experiments produced PulseTriage: sparse regression localization from scalar rollback outcomes.
survived: Designed interventions plus one scalar consequence can localize scarce useful action.
killed: The original image task had averaging shortcuts exposed by trivial attackers.

claim: Sampling policy, shared traces and slow material infrastructure shape later computation and organization.
survived: History can harden into slower external structure that causally changes later dynamics.
killed: Simple refractory stigmergy diversified sampling while harming prediction; lineage is not heredity.

claim: Prediction/observation loop where inference changes the state from which the next observation is made.
survived: Active sensing and persistent trace as computational variables.
killed: Not treated as a finished general intelligence architecture.

claim: Structured local/splat representation line later reused as a shared latent/world substrate.
survived: World/image state assembled from many local structured elements.
killed: Visual coherence alone is not proof of correct 3-D geometry.

claim: Continuation of the splat-world line toward richer image/world latents.
survived: Local structured representation and addressable latent manipulation.
killed: Detailed causal claims still require deeper re-audit.

claim: Trained image decoder whose Jacobian/pin-driver became a concrete write operator downstream.
survived: A learned decoder supplies measurable state-dependent J for read/write experiments.
killed: Low-rank decoder Jacobian alone is not a general world model.

claim: Separates world belief from external support/provenance while keeping experimental branches reproducible.
survived: Observed versus imagined state is explicit bookkeeping; failed branches remain controls.
killed: RGB-only coherent rotation did not establish correct geometry.

claim: Moved from failed partial reconstruction to response geometry: high-rank J, low-rank local Delta J, overlap-dependent interference.
survived: Changes to a large operator may be much more compressible than the operator itself.
killed: Tiny-fragment hologram/reconstruction and long-range amplification stories did not survive.

claim: Address-conditioned operator experiments connect stored structure with different effective transformations.
survived: A fixed substrate can expose different effective operators under different addresses.
killed: Detailed claims still need deeper re-audit.

claim: Asks what population/search dynamics leave behind as reusable modes/routes, not only optimization outcomes.
survived: Search trajectory as a source of reusable structure and mode separation.
killed: Ordinary GA was not accepted as literally identical to JKO/Wasserstein flow.

claim: Fusion branch around search, causal consequences and protection of existing computation.
survived: Counterfactual/causal structure can constrain updates and expose collisions.
killed: The line moved beyond a simple GA-plus-linear-transform story.

claim: Transformer experiments asking how trained forward computation branches/routes and can be perturbed.
survived: Forward computation as deformable routing rather than backprop being the computation.
killed: Dendritic analogies remain abstractions, not identity claims.

claim: Oja mode selection, branched dynamics, nonlinear subunits and slow structural/operator adaptation tested as separable mechanisms.
survived: A falsifiable neuron-inspired decomposition with retained failures.
killed: A strong synthetic local rule did not generalize across 24 worlds; growth-depth still uses oracle target purity.

claim: Developmental bridge: grow sparse wiring, compile receiver cables, then shuffle address-to-operator assignments on fixed anatomy.
survived: Developmental address, input port and physical operator identity are separable variables.
killed: The v2 operator codebook was an oracle calibration and gave no broad functional advantage.

claim: Separates maintained vector state from sparse innovation events and slower persistence adaptation.
survived: Resident state can be synchronized with fewer transmissions while preserving most task quality.
killed: Local RMS homeostasis was not automatically task-optimal.

claim: Separates resident-state repair from publication control and adds a predictive receiver.
survived: Reliability, resident computation and causal publication are distinct when state has memory.
killed: A single signed scalar reproduced the earlier exclusive two-channel task; factorization mattered only with overlapping constraints.

claim: Converges resident dynamics, late relevance, sparse publication and routed local writes.
survived: State is not current relevance; resident hidden processes may improve readiness after context switches.
killed: Current v3 comparison is confounded because the generic RNN baseline also trained worse.
